### Recommendation

For your specific use case involving 10 GB of newline-delimited JSON logs, I strongly recommend using Zstandard at compression level 3. This choice optimally balances the competing demands of compression ratio and decompression speed, which are critical since the archives will be decompressed repeatedly after a single write operation. While gzip level 6 offers a mature, widely supported standard, Zstandard significantly outperforms it in both compression efficiency and, more importantly, decompression throughput. Given that your logs contain repetitive structural elements like field names and standardized timestamps, Zstandard’s superior entropy coding and dictionary capabilities will capture these patterns more effectively than gzip, resulting in smaller file sizes without sacrificing the rapid access speeds needed for frequent log interrogation.

### Supporting basis

The primary advantage lies in Zstandard’s asymmetric design: level 3 achieves a very fast compression speed suitable for single-threaded archival while providing a much faster decompression rate than gzip. This is crucial because decompression happens repeatedly, making its speed the dominant performance factor for your workflow. JLNImplicitly, the repeated field names and consistent structure in JSON logs create high redundancy. Zstandard’s internal dictionary matchers exploit this locality better than gzip’s sliding window model. Benchmarks consistently show Zstandard level 3 compressing JSON data to smaller sizes than gzip level 6, often with 2-3x faster decompression. Although gzip is universally available, installing Zstandard is trivial in modern environments. For a one-time write where long-term storage efficiency and read performance matter, Zstandard’s mathematical superiority in handling repetitive text data makes it the unequivocally better practical choice over gzip’s legacy algorithm.<|im_end|>
